<security_assessment>

<details>
The PKGBUILD contains no top-level command substitutions, dynamic version functions, or other code that would execute during sourcing beyond simple variable assignments and array definitions. All source URLs point to the project's own GitHub repository (raw.githubusercontent.com and github.com releases), which is standard for AUR packages. The checksums are provided (not SKIP). LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is a standard AUR binary package for the zepto terminal text editor. It downloads a pre-built binary and documentation files from the official GitHub repository (joewalnes/zepto) and installs them to standard locations. No evidence of malicious behavior is present: there is no data exfiltration, no obfuscated code, no execution of unexpected remote scripts, and no tampering with unrelated system files.

A few unusual aspects are noted but do not constitute genuine threats: (1) the pkgver is set to a future date (2026.08.30), which is unconventional but not malicious in AUR context; (2) the url field points to https://zepto.now/ rather than the GitHub upstream, which is odd but harmless metadata; (3) the package depends on perl despite the description claiming "no dependencies," which is a documentation discrepancy rather than a security issue. The download source is the project's own GitHub releases, which is expected and appropriate.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>
Standard AUR binary package with no malicious indicators found.
</summary>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a `.SRCINFO` metadata file for the `zepto-bin` AUR package. It contains only package metadata: name, description, dependencies, source URLs, and their corresponding SHA256 checksums. No SOURCE entries use `SKIP` for their checksums; all ten sources have valid 64-character SHA256 hashes listed.

All source URLs point to the project's own upstream repository (`joewalnes/zepto` on GitHub, both raw file URLs and the GitHub releases page). The sources are pinned to a specific commit identifier (`bb29170`), and they include documentation files (LICENSE, README, BUGS, CLAUDE, DESIGN, FEATURES, ABOUT, TUTORIAL, CHANGELOG) and the main `zepto` binary from the releases page. There is no obfuscated code, no `eval`, no `base64`-encoded blobs, no `curl|bash` patterns, and no unexpected network destinations. A `.SRCINFO` file is pure metadata with no executable logic, and nothing here deviates from standard packaging practices.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
SRCINFO metadata is benign with pinned, checksummed upstream sources
</summary>
</security_assessment>
